newsitem.title: JAPAN: New Tokyo mall gets 350,000 visitors on first day.
newsitem.headline: New Tokyo mall gets 350,000 visitors on first day.

text.p: Ritzy Japanese department store operator Takashimaya Co Ltd opened a giant shopping mall in central Tokyo on Friday, and said the number of visitors on the first day surpassed the company's expectations.

Takashimaya, Japan's oldest department store operator, said an estimated 350,000 people visited its "Times Square" building on Friday, with about 10,000 lining up in the morning to wait for the opening of the mall.
The company had expected 300,000 people on opening day.

The shopping mall, which comprises a Takashimaya department store, large book and music stores, an indoor amusement park, beauty parlours, a 3-D theatre and other facilities, opened in Shinjuku, one of Tokyo's busiest shopping districts.
The company is investing 160 billion yen ($1.44 billion) in the 55,000 square metre mall (590,000 square feet), which has 11 floors.
Sales at the Takashimaya department store portion of the mall on the opening day alone were estimated at two billion yen ($18.0 million), a spokesman for Takashimaya said.
The company has forecast sales at its Shinjuku store at 80 billion yen ($720 million) in the initial year of operation.
Analysts say the Takashimaya mall has ignited fierce competition among retailers because it will lead to a drop in sales of other department stores in Shinjuku and neighbouring areas.
As a counter-measure to try to hold on to customers, retailers nearby are expanding their selling space and introducing new brands.
There are at least five other department stores in Shinjuku.
